name: Dodge / Avoid
subtitle: Survive under continuous pressure and spatial constraints; the core revolves around hit detection, windows, and rhythm.
demoRuleHint: Rule: Hazard generation → Warning/trajectory → Player movement → Hit detection (hit/near miss) → Feedback (damage/Invincibility frames)
problemsSolved: Make failure reasons attributable (why you were hit, where safety lies)
Turn near misses into satisfying moments rather than just staying alive
Control intensity with a pressure curve (density/velocity/rhythm) to avoid pure numeric stacking
learningGoals: Understand how sources of pressure and rhythm shape difficulty
Master hit detection and tolerance (near miss/Invincibility frames/slowing)
minimalRules: Movement: Player movement and constraints (speed, turning, boundaries)
Hit detection: Hit radius and resolution (damage/failure/Invincibility frames)
systemLoopHint: Input (movement/dodging) → Prediction (read warning) → Hit detection (hit/near miss) → Feedback (damage/survival) → Pressure change → New input

combos.effect: Output while evading, creating a 'positioning and shooting' loop
Convert survival time/perfect dodges into progression resources
Randomize hazard patterns, emphasizing adaptation and reading the map

advancedWarnings: Unclear warnings make failures unaccountable (players feel unjustified)
Too fast speed with weak feedback turns the experience into 'passively getting hit'
Overly strict hit detection compresses expressive space; overly lenient loses tension
advancedAlgoRefs: Generation: Bullet/obstacle generator and difficulty curve
Hit detection: Circle/capsule collision, near-miss detection, invincibility frame window

demoLab.title: Hit Tolerance Experiment
demoLab.action: Drag "Forgiveness Window (hitbox shrink, px)" from 0 up to 24, then deliberately let bullets graze past your ship
demoLab.observe: Tolerance = the hitbox is one ring smaller than the visuals: at 0px a graze kills, at 24px players dare to thread between bullets. The gap between the two circles is your near-miss budget — too strict crushes showmanship, too loose kills the tension

demoLab.title: Near-Miss Reward Experiment
demoLab.action: Pull "Graze Bonus" from 0 to 50, then set "Bullet Density" to 3+ and actively fly close to bullets
demoLab.observe: A graze bonus turns dodging from survival into a chased thrill: hazards become score resources. The higher the reward, the closer players hug danger — one parameter rewrites the whole risk-reward curve

demoLab.title: Density Pressure Curve
demoLab.action: Step "Bullet Density" from 1 up to 5, surviving 20 seconds at each level
demoLab.observe: Density is the pressure-curve knob: each +1 visibly shrinks the safe space ratio. Density alone is not difficulty — real difficulty is density × tolerance: dense + forgiving stays casual, sparse + strict still kills
